units.text: Start with the left panel: a customer managed KMS key can use AWS generated or imported key material, so material origin does not determine key ownership.
The middle panel keeps the KMS interface but uses a connected CloudHSM cluster, making cluster availability and capacity part of the design.
Follow the right panel through the external key store proxy to the external key manager, where supported cryptographic operations introduce additional latency and availability dependencies.
With the full slide visible, separate ownership, material origin, and execution location, and plan recovery for imported material before it expires or is deleted.
Compare the two paths on the left: the upper connection terminates TLS at the Application Load Balancer, while the lower connection terminates at the EC2 application server.
Follow the upper right chain from the application server through its supported client and provider stack to CloudHSM for private key operations.
The lower right panel lists the operational dependencies: cluster availability, client configuration, private connectivity, certificate deployment, and application recovery.
Returning to the full slide, identify where TLS terminates and which system uses the private key, because CloudHSM is not a transparent network proxy.
